clue.text: Famous rider to hold in the highest esteem

definitions.meaning: Paul ... made a celebrated midnight ride in 1775 to warn of British troops

definitions.text: to hold in the highest esteem
definitions.meaning: to venerate or honour someone deeply

explanation.surface: A celebrated horseman is someone we greatly admire.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere is the American patriot famed for his ride; as a verb the word means to venerate.

clue.text: Clicked on leaving transport?

definitions.meaning: stepped down from a bus or train

explanation.surface: Someone pressed a button while stepping off a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clicked on' suggests a computer mouse; 'on' is only a link word between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a couple who hit it off romantically are said to have paired up this way; alighting from a vehicle is the literal sense.

clue.text: They're responsible for bars being notably crowded

definitions.text: They're responsible for bars being notably crowded

parts.words: They're responsible for bars being notably crowded
parts.note: bars here are musical measures, and 'notably' means full of notes: the very shortest notes pack a bar most densely

explanation.surface: Something seems to blame for pubs being packed.
explanation.definitionFit: These thirty-second notes are so brief that a bar of music written in them holds a great many symbols.

clue.text: Clerical office ready-made round the Durham area

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the other piece, enclosing it
ready-made is read as 'ready' being made up anew, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Durham lies in England's North East, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A church post comes off the peg in County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready-made' reads as one adjective, but 'made' is the anagram signal on the word before it, and 'round' is the container signal; County Durham is in the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean's office or position in the church hierarchy goes by this name, as does his residence.

clue.text: Of course it's outside the normal timetable

definitions.text: Of course it's outside the normal timetable

parts.words: Of course it's outside the normal timetable
parts.note: 'Of course' looks like an interjection but means 'relating to a course of study': an activity beyond that course

explanation.surface: Naturally, something does not run to the usual schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs and sports held beyond the school curriculum are described by this word.

clue.text: Barrie's admirable butler

parts.note: J. M. Barrie's 1902 play is named after its resourceful manservant, called 'The Admirable' in the title

explanation.surface: A playwright praises his excellent manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Barrie's play The Admirable Crichton is a butler who takes charge on a desert island.

clue.text: Heretical creeds on the black list

indicators.note: heretical beliefs depart from orthodoxy, so these letters depart from their order

explanation.surface: Unorthodox doctrines have been banned by the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heretical' rearranges CREEDS and ON; the definition is read as 'on the black list', with 'on' doing duty in the fodder, a loose setter's touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Material suppressed by a censor is effectively banned, as anything blacklisted would be.

clue.text: Italian painter singled out in poetry

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: poetry is verse
something singled out is the one picked

explanation.surface: An Italian artist gets special mention in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a sixteenth-century Venetian painter of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Warrior king cross and hesitant with the opposite sex

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
er is a hesitant sound

indicators.note: the opposite way round, so the word sex is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fighting monarch is angry and shy around women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the opposite sex' looks like a phrase about women; 'the opposite' reverses SEX to XES.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes I was the Persian king who invaded Greece in 480 BC.

clue.text: Island for which Cockneys express dislike

indicators.note: Cockneys (Londoners of the East End) drop the H, so the word for dislike is heard spoken their way

parts.note: dislike is hate; spoken by a Cockney it comes out as 'ate

explanation.surface: Londoners voice hostility towards a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: An ait or eyot is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Feeling for one to reciprocate in the West country

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Devon is a county in the West Country of England

indicators.note: to reciprocate is to go back the other way, so these two words are read backwards

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: Affection for someone returned in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reciprocate' turns 'one to' around, giving OTI; the West Country is England's south-western counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is deep loyalty or affection felt for someone.

clue.text: Man of figures among the others changed roles

indicators.note: one piece goes among the letters of the other

parts.note: the rest means the others
a CA, chartered accountant, works with figures

explanation.surface: An accountant among the cast members swapped parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To recast a play is to give its parts to different actors.

clue.text: Has deep personal regrets about evil

definitions.text: Has deep personal regrets about evil

parts.words: Has deep personal regrets about evil
parts.note: read as describing someone who disapproves of their own failings, belittling oneself

explanation.surface: Someone feels profound remorse over wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-deprecating person plays down their own worth, deprecating meaning disapproving.

clue.text: Young skipper, we hear, hard to beat

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for young skipper is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a lamb is a young animal that skips

explanation.surface: A junior captain sounds hard to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young skipper' looks like a boat's captain; it is a lamb skipping in a field. 'hard' qualifies the definition: to lam is to beat hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is a slang verb meaning to thrash or wallop.

clue.text: Cotton material from a large part of Cambridge, note

indicators.note: only a large part of the town name is used, its end dropped

parts.note: C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Fabric sourced from much of a university city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven linen or cotton cloth.

clue.text: Military expedition on a North American footing

parts.note: a footing is a basis

explanation.surface: A campaign is planned on an American basis.
explanation.definitionFit: An anabasis is a march upcountry, after Xenophon's account of a Greek army's campaign.

clue.text: To hospital doctors on their rounds they're of signal importance

definitions.text: To hospital doctors on their rounds they're of signal importance

parts.words: To hospital doctors on their rounds they're of signal importance
parts.note: 'signal importance' means great importance but also literally importance as signals: pagers summoning medics

explanation.surface: Things matter a lot to doctors doing ward rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagers that beep to summon staff were essential kit for hospital doctors.

clue.text: A danger averted in the West Indies

indicators.note: averted means turned aside, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A threat was avoided in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the island by where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean, part of the West Indies.

clue.text: Title held by one in 28

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the answer to 28 across

parts.note: the solution to 28 across, which contains these letters

explanation.surface: A champion's crown is held by someone in clue 28.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 28 across, made capital of, holds the three letters in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali held boxing's world heavyweight title three times.

clue.text: It gives me a certain standard

parts.note: taken as written
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Something provides me with a definite benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a yardstick or standard by which things are judged.

clue.text: What makes a chauvinist feel he's better?

definitions.text: What makes a chauvinist feel he's better?

parts.words: What makes a chauvinist feel he's better?
parts.note: a sexist man's belief that his own sex outranks women

explanation.surface: Why does a bigot think he is superior?
explanation.definitionFit: A male chauvinist holds that men rank above women.

clue.text: Showed bad taste having taken over at Scotland Yard

parts.note: ran, as in took charge of
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is based at Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters

explanation.surface: Someone acted tastelessly after taking command at police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: rancid food shows a bad taste. Scotland Yard is London's Metropolitan Police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter or fat gone rancid has a sour, off flavour.

clue.text: Daisy Bell's revolutionary bridal carriage

parts.note: the song Daisy Bell promises 'a bicycle built for two' for the wedding; revolutionary means with wheels that turn

explanation.surface: A girl's radical wedding coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-seater bicycle of the song is one where riders sit one behind the other.

clue.text: World chess champion making a move in park at the centre of Hove

indicators.note: the letters of park move about into a new order
the middle letters of the town name are taken

explanation.surface: A grandmaster plays a move in a park in Hove.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatoly Karpov was world chess champion from 1975 to 1985.

clue.text: Very attractive lady of habit writhing in pain

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so these letters are twisted

parts.note: a nun wears a habit

explanation.surface: A gorgeous nun twists about in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' rearranges NUN to UNN, which goes 'in' STING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunning means strikingly beautiful.

clue.text: English copper coin once of gold and silver in France

definitions.text: coin once of gold and silver in France

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An English copper coin, formerly gold and silver, in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecu was an old French coin minted in gold and later silver.

clue.text: "To hold, as 'twere, the up to nature" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "To hold, as 'twere, the up to nature" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "To hold, as 'twere, the up to nature" (Hamlet)
parts.note: Hamlet's advice to the players, with the missing object of 'hold' to be supplied

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet says acting's purpose is to show nature its own reflection, like a looking-glass.

clue.text: Saw the light and made capital out of it

explanation.surface: Someone had a revelation and profited from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise is both to come to understand and to turn property into money.
